1480	It is customary to take the cup of the head of the family, the one who leads the Seder, takes his cup of wine
1481	and drips from it.
1482	and drips from it. The custom is to use either a broken vessel or a disposable
1483	vessel that is thrown away afterward. Some pour it out
1484	into the drain, the sink,
1485	the toilet, and then he says the order: blood,
1486	frog, lice, wild beasts. There is a segulah in this for nullifying all
1487	kinds of decrees; everything goes with this wine to destruction.
1488	Also when he says the acronyms Detzakh Adash B'achav: blood,
1489	and fire and pillars of smoke too, in total 16 times
1490	he drips: blood and fire and pillars of smoke, Detzakh Adash B'achav,
1491	for there are secrets in the acronyms of the ten plagues.
1492	Then blood, frog, the ten plagues, all 16
1493	he drips. It is important
1494	to remember that the main mitzvah on the night of the Seder is "and you shall tell your son."
1495	And we have a few more mitzvot that every person from Bar
1496	Mitzvah age must be careful with. One mitzvah is to eat
1497	at least
1498	a kezayit
1499	of matzah that is guarded for the sake of the mitzvah of matzah.
1500	Shmurah matzah means that from the time
1501	of the harvest they guarded the flour so that not a drop of
1502	water would fall on it. So it is important to be careful to use shmurah matzah. There is machine-made
1503	shmurah, written on the box "shmurah"; there is
1504	handmade shmurah matzah, which is ideal. It does cost
1505	more, but it is worth buying for the Seder. All Pesach
1506	one may eat regular matzah, but on the night of the Seder one must
1507	be careful as much as possible to buy handmade matzot
1508	with a good kashrut certification, and to fulfill the mitzvah of eating a kezayit of matzah,
1509	men and women alike, from Bar Mitzvah age and up
1510	or Bat Mitzvah, with handmade matzot, because
1511	in handmade matzot there is the "for its own sake," for the sake of the mitzvah of matzah.
1512	And machine matzot,
1513	the machine does make it; the one who presses the button
1514	says "for the sake of the mitzvah of matzah," but it is not the same
1515	as a person who makes it with his hands and says "for the sake of the matzah
1516	mitzvah." So on the night of the Seder it is important to be careful with handmade
1517	matzot. So we eat at least one kezayit. A kezayit
1518	is 28 grams. Whoever does not know such measures
1519	should weigh it at noon; one can weigh with a kezayit scale.
